title: Log Bash Commands
summary: A Claude Code hook that appends every shell command the agent runs to .claude/command-log.txt with a timestamp, for review afterward.
description: When an agent works for a while it is hard to remember what it ran. This PreToolUse hook writes each Bash command to a plain text log next to your project settings.
Each line holds an ISO timestamp and the command as a JSON string, so multi-line commands stay on one line. Nothing leaves your machine.
useWhen: Audit what an agent ran during a long session
Reconstruct the steps that fixed a problem
Review commands before you trust a workflow
Keep a record for a team or compliance

example.prompt: Run the tests and fix any failures.
example.result: .claude/command-log.txt gains lines such as: 2026-11-15T09:12:44.120Z "npm test". Add the file to .gitignore if you do not want to commit it.

faq.question: Where is the log?
faq.answer: In .claude/command-log.txt under the folder Claude Code was started in.

faq.question: Does it block anything?
faq.answer: No. It always lets the command run and only writes the line.
